The '''Moschovakis coding lemma''' is a [[Lemma (mathematics)|lemma]] from descriptive [[set theory]] involving sets of [[real number]]s under the [[axiom of determinacy]] (the principle — incompatible with [[Axiom of choice|choice]] — that every two-player integer game is determined). The lemma was developed and named after the mathematician [[Yiannis N. Moschovakis]].

The lemma may be expressed generally as follows:
:Let {{mvar|Γ}} be a non-selfdual [[pointclass]] closed under [[Quantifier (logic)#Range of quantification|real quantification]] and {{math|∧}}, and {{math|≺}} a {{mvar|Γ}}-well-founded relation on {{math|''ω<sup>ω</sup>''}} of rank {{math|''θ'' ∈ ON}}. Let {{math|R ⊆ dom(≺) × ''ω<sup>ω</sup>''}} be such that {{math|(∀''x''∈dom(≺))(∃''y'')(''x'' R ''y'')}}.  Then there is a {{mvar|Γ}}-set {{math|A ⊆ dom(≺) × ''ω<sup>ω</sup>''}} which is a [[choice set]] for R, that is: 
<!--Note that the specific numbering of these properties is used in the proof below.-->
# {{math|(∀''α''<''θ'')(∃''x''∈dom(≺),''y'')({{mabs|''x''}}<sub>≺</sub>{{=}}''α'' ∧ ''x'' A ''y'')}}.
# {{math|(∀''x'',''y'')(''x'' A ''y'' → ''x'' R ''y'')}}.
A proof runs as follows: suppose for contradiction {{mvar|θ}} is a minimal counterexample, and fix {{math|≺}}, {{math|R}}, and a good universal set {{math|''U'' ⊆ (''ω<sup>ω</sup>'')<sup>3</sup>}} for the {{mvar|Γ}}-subsets of {{math|(''ω<sup>ω</sup>'')<sup>2</sup>}}.  Easily, {{mvar|θ}} must be a limit ordinal. For {{math|''δ'' < ''θ''}}, we say {{math|''u'' ∈ ''ω<sup>ω</sup>''}} codes a {{mvar|δ}}-choice set provided the property (1) holds for {{math|''α'' ≤ ''δ''}} using {{math|A {{=}} ''U u''}} and property (2) holds for {{math|A {{=}} ''U u''}} where we replace {{math|''x'' ∈ dom(≺)}} with {{math|''x'' ∈ dom(≺) ∧ {{mabs|''x''}} ≺ [≤''δ'']}}.  By minimality of {{mvar|θ}}, for all {{math|''δ'' < ''θ''}}, there are {{math|δ}}-choice sets.

Now, play a game where players I, II select points {{math|''u'',''v'' ∈ ''ω<sup>ω</sup>''}} and II wins when {{mvar|u}} coding a {{math|''δ''<sub>1</sub>}}-choice set for some {{math|''δ''<sub>1</sub> < ''θ''}} implies {{mvar|v}} codes a {{math|''δ''<sub>2</sub>}}-choice set for some {{math|''δ''<sub>2</sub> > ''δ''<sub>1</sub>}}.  A winning strategy for I defines a {{math|Σ{{su|b=1|p=1}}}} set {{mvar|B}} of reals encoding {{mvar|δ}}-choice sets for arbitrarily large {{math|''δ'' < ''θ''}}.  Define then 
:{{math|''x'' A ''y'' ↔ (∃''w''∈''B'')''U''(''w'',''x'',''y'')}},
which easily works.  On the other hand, suppose {{mvar|τ}} is a winning strategy for II.  From the [[Smn theorem|{{subsup|S|n|m}} theorem]], let {{math|''s'':(''ω<sup>ω</sup>'')<sup>2</sup> → ''ω<sup>ω</sup>''}} be continuous such that for all {{mvar|ϵ}}, {{mvar|x}}, {{mvar|t}}, and {{mvar|w}}, 
:{{math|''U''(''s''(''ϵ'',''x''),''t'',''w'') ↔ (∃''y'',''z'')(''y'' ≺ ''x'' ∧ ''U''(''ϵ'',''y'',''z'') ∧ ''U''(''z'',''t'',''w''))}}.  
By the recursion theorem, there exists {{math|''ϵ''<sub>0</sub>}} such that {{math|''U''(''ϵ''<sub>0</sub>,''x'',''z'') ↔ ''z'' {{=}} ''τ''(''s''(''ϵ''<sub>0</sub>,''x''))}}.  A straightforward induction on {{math|{{mabs|''x''}}<sub>≺</sub>}} for {{math|''x'' ∈ dom(≺)}} shows that 
:{{math|(∀''x''∈dom(≺))(∃!''z'')''U''(''ϵ''<sub>0</sub>,''x'',''z'')}}, 
and 
:{{math|(∀''x''∈dom(≺),''z'')(''U''(''ϵ''<sub>0</sub>,''x'',''z'') → ''z'' encodes a choice set of ordinal ≥{{mabs|x}}<sub>≺</sub>)}}. 
So let 
:{{math|''x'' A ''y'' ↔ (∃''z''∈dom(≺),''w'')(''U''(''ϵ''<sub>0</sub>,''z'',''w'') ∧ ''U''(''w'',''x'',''y''))}}.<ref>{{cite book
